item: A shipped stoplist change reaches the stored top keywords and the cached Home cards (R111 step T3)
summary: A fingerprint of the shipped stoplist decides when the stored Article.top_keyword_id/count/tied_n are recomputed (only for articles whose top set held a hidden word, a non-lowest tie member included; three columns only, updated_at untouched, no mention row moves) by one resumable job in the off-peak window and its offline timer, each chunk one short transaction sized to hold the write window about a quarter of a second, stopping at a chunk boundary for the storage or memory guard, the fingerprint recorded only after the last chunk. The Home cache carries the fingerprint it was made under and refreshes through the existing background path when it differs. A word taken off the list is walked as a restored keyword so the tops made without it are recomputed; every list a pass walks is recorded before its first chunk commits, and the finished fingerprint also lives in the database, so a stopped pass, a restore or a moved database never leaves a hidden word in a top (an unknown baseline walks without the shortcut, once); the keyword fold computes the stored top without the shipped list's words, and a merge that carries articles forgets the finished run so the next window walks without the shortcut once. Measured on a 200,000-article synthetic store: 6 to 11 s plaintext and 7 to 11 s as an encrypted copy (SQLCipher) with a known baseline, 14 s the first time with none, the write window held 0.28 to 0.39 s from gate to commit, log high-water under 5 MiB, no temp b-tree, and an independent recompute matched on every article; the in-pass memory is capped at 500,000 ids (about 31 MiB) and a smaller cap only slows the pass.
